header.title: Lucidarius (Gö1) (Göttingen, Staats- und Universitätsbibl., 2° Cod. Ms. theol. 101n Cim.): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Anonymous
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rem:anonymous:m132g:norm, from the Referenzkorpus Mittelhochdeutsch, ReM 2.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.1v.3: The 'belts' (strâze, lit. 'roads') of 1v.3 are the climatic zones of the world. 1v.18 gives Ganges for Gihon as well, probably in error for the Nile, which the master names below. Normenia (1v.30) is read as Armenia; Môrlant (1v.28), the land of the Moors, is Ethiopia. 'sunder' (1v.31, 1v.38) taken as 'southward'; it could mean 'separately'. Orkobare and Parchoatra are kept as written.
notes.1r.14: The text's Jobel, Jobal and Neomina are given as the biblical Jabal, Jubal and Naamah; the third brother (Tubal-cain) is not named. 'êre' (1r.23) taken as bronze or brass.

nodes.text: dries up in the sun. Then the pupil said: How would people have begotten children
if they had stood firm in paradise? Then the master said: As when one lays two hands
together, without desire and without sin. Then the pupil said: How long did Adam live? Then the master said:
Nine hundred years and thirty years. Then he died at Jerusalem; afterwards he was buried
in Hebron, and the same pit was filled with him from which he had been
made. Then the pupil said: How old was Abel when his brother slew him? Then the master said: When he was thirty
years old he was slain at Damascus. Then the pupil said: Who was the first man who ever
began [to make] tents? Then the master said: That was Jabal, Lamech's son. He had a brother who
was called Jubal; he was the first who ever invented music. The third brother was the first
man who ever began to forge with iron and with bronze. These same three brothers had a
sister called Naamah; she first of all found the skill by which people began
to weave. Then the pupil said: Who was the first king after the Flood? Then the master said: That was
Shem, Noah's son, who was later called Melchizedek. In that king's time
people were divided into three: from Shem came the free, from Japheth came
note that of this world nothing is inhabited except the third part, as
is painted there before you. Then the pupil said: How is that same
third part divided that we inhabit? Then the master said:
The world is divided into three. The one is called
Asia, the second is called Europe, the
third is called Africa. Then the pupil said: Now
tell me of the part that is called
Asia. Then the master said: Asia begins where
the sun rises, and runs on the north side
to the sea. In that part is paradise,
right where the sun rises. In paradise
a spring wells up, out of which [flow]
four rivers. The one is called Pishon in paradise;
when it comes out from there it is called Ganges. The second is called
Gihon; when it comes out of paradise it is called Ganges. The third
is called Tigris, the fourth Euphrates. These two do not change their names.
Then the pupil said: Do the rivers run through paradise? Then the master said: The two rivers are
so great that if they ran through paradise they would ruin a great part of it. That is why the books tell
us that the rivers run in paradise under the earth. When they then
come out from there, they break out over the earth. Then the pupil said: Now tell me where
the rivers rise. Then the master said: The one is called Ganges; it rises in India
from a mountain called Orkobare and flows eastward into the encircling ocean.
The second is called Nile; it rises from a mountain called Atlas and
at once sinks into the earth as far as the Red Sea; there it has two sources,
and so it flows through the land of the Moors and through Egypt; there it gains seven mouths
down to Alexandria, where it falls into the great sea. Tigris and Euphrates
both rise in Armenia from a mountain called Parchoatra
and both flow southward into the sea. Then the pupil said: Which land lies to paradise
nearest of all? Then the master said: As the books say, into paradise no one can
come except by good works. A wall runs round it which reaches to
heaven; before it stand mountains and forests. After that lies a great wilderness, which is full of
dragons and beasts; for that reason no one can get through it. After that lies a land
nearest of all, which is called India. The land is named after a river that is called
Indus, which rises from a mountain called Caucasus. The river
flows southward to the Red Sea. The land is hard to get into, for on one side
